story: [[c:Oundle, 1626. The Talbot inn is being rebuilt in fine stone, and carts have been bringing stone from the ruins of Fotheringhay Castle, where Mary, Queen of Scots, was executed.]]
[[c:With the stone came a carved oak crown, said to be from the staircase the Queen walked down on her last morning. The landlord meant to set it on his new staircase.]]
[[c:Last night the old well in the inn yard began to drum, as people say it does before trouble. By morning the oak crown was gone.]]

[[c:Four people were about the yard that night: Silas Webb, the master mason; Tom Crane, a boy from Laxton's school; Martha Pell, the carter who brought the stone; and Josiah Gant, landlord of a rival inn. Find out who took the crown, and why.]]

start_page.support: [[c:Support the town: there are cafés, pubs and independent shops around the Market Place. The short walk takes about 45 minutes to 1 hour 15; the long walk about 1 hour 30 to 2 hours.]]
